newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-CENTURY FOR AZHARUDDIN AS INDIA DRAW TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CENTURY FOR AZHARUDDIN AS INDIA DRAW TEST.

text.p: Mohammad Azharuddin hit his 19th test century to help India draw the second and final test against Sri Lanka on Wednesday.
India, set 373 runs off a minimum of 103 overs to win, never attempted to reach the target and finished on 281 for five.
The first test was also drawn.
Sri Lanka took two wickets in each of the first two sessions, but Azharuddin, veteran of 85 tests, scored an unbeaten 108 to deny the home side victory.
The 34-year-old right-hander gave three chances while steering India to safety in an 175-ball innings that included 14 fours.

Off-spinner Muthiah Muralitharan dropped a hard return catch from Azharuddin, while wicketkeeper Romesh Kaluwitharana put down a simple chance when the former Indian captain attempted to cut Sanath Jayasuriya and got an outside edge.
Jayasuriya himself then also missed a caught and bowled chance.
Azharuddin shared a 110-run fifth wicket partnership with left-hander Saurav Ganguly which put the match out of Sri Lanka's reach.
Sri Lanka began the day promisingly by taking the wickets of Navjot Sidhu for 16 in the fourth over of the day and Rahul Dravid for six soon afterwards to leave India on 75 for two.
Further success followed when Muralitheran dismissed Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar for eight and Sajeeva de Silva had opener Ajay Jadeja caught in the gully for 73.
But Sri Lanka had to wait another 132 minutes before any further success. That came with the dismissal of Ganguly for 45, caught behind off Muralitheran, but by then India were safe from defeat.
Aravinda de Silva, with a century in each innings, was name man of the match and Sanath Jayasuriya, with a batting average of 190.33, was adjudged the man of the series.
